post.description:
Always refuses. A prepared proposal is a reviewed plan, not an authorization.

The refusal happens before any provider I/O, and is reached only after the
proposal is proven to exist in this workspace, so callers cannot use this
operation to probe another workspace. A later release may admit an
execution capability; until then there is no code path that purchases.
